I will keep my land in the usual Quzhou grain rotation: winter wheat followed by summer maize. In my county, wheat and maize are the safest crops for me because the land, machines, water setup, and selling channels all match them, and most fields around me are run this way. I do not want to gamble on crops that need more market judgment or more hand labor. I am 56, so I would rather grow crops I know well, keep the work rhythm steady, and protect yield first.

I will manage the field with lower-input but still stable production. For wheat, I will use improved seed, rotary till before sowing, put on enough nitrogen but not the old heavy rate, and keep phosphorus and potassium balanced so the crop stands well and fills grain. Wheat needs my irrigation more than maize here, so I will water it twice at the key stages and spray a couple of times to hold disease and weeds down. After wheat harvest, I will plant summer maize right away, mostly with no-tillage so I do not lose time or moisture. Summer rain does a lot of the work here, so I will only plan one irrigation for maize unless the season turns dry. I will use hybrid maize seed for better yield, keep fertilizer moderate, and do two pesticide passes because I do not want weeds or insects to take the crop. I am aiming for steady grain, lower waste, and less water use, not chasing the very highest possible yield.
